cells.tense: You're keeping the private scale, and it's steady — what's right shows up in the body before it shows up in words.
cells.ask: Name one thing that's already finished as finished, and let what still stands be counted without re-checking it.
cells.core:
You're the one holding the scale, and holding it doesn't take much from you right now. What's fair and what's owed arrives without a fight; you feel it and you act from it, mostly without announcing it. Standing where the pull wants you to go, you're free — nothing about the direction is being forced, and nothing about it has to be defended. That quiet steadiness is the thing under everything else you're carrying today.

It's fed by what's already over. The scale doesn't need old accounts reopened to prove it still reads true; the proof is the way you move today. Let what's finished stay finished. What's still standing is where the next good thing gets counted, and there's more of it than you've been letting yourself see.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's fair without needing to calculate it.
cells.verb: Weighing what's fair in the body, before any argument arrives
cells.place: in the pull toward the light you're steering by

cells.tense: You're already at a verdict that hasn't happened yet, rehearsing a fairness nobody has asked you for.
cells.ask: Pick one person whose weight you've been holding early, and let your strength sit beside their load today instead of inside it.
cells.core:
At its cleanest, this is the compass pointing toward morning — you feel what's fair in the moment it matters and lift only what you've actually been given to carry. The pull toward light stays clean because your strength is out at the edge, holding what's already here and nothing else.

What's running now is the scale ahead of the moment — what will be owed, who will be unfair, what you'll have to set right. The direction is still there, but it's dragging a need to have everything settled before it arrives. Fairness you can't put down stops being fairness and starts being a debt you owe yourself, and the debt comes due before anything has happened.

cells.tense: You're still turned toward a moment when your sense of right went quiet, and you're taking your instructions from back there.
cells.ask: Take one small practice you can return to before tonight, and let it be the directions back into what you already know.
cells.core:
In its best shape, the compass simply points — you feel what's fair, you say it plainly, and the pull toward light stays fed because the knowing is moving through you instead of sitting still. That shape isn't far off. It's the same compass, just allowed to speak.

Something in you still knows what's fair. That sense never left — it just hasn't been handed the wheel, and the direction goes unfed without it. Careful has been standing in for sure, and careful starts to look like standing still. The way in isn't to feel your way back into the pull. It's one small disciplined step, today, that the scale can come back online under — a practice, a rhythm, a plain instruction you can follow.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's fair. You just stopped acting like it.

cells.tense: The weighing is running right now, in your own body, and you're talking about it as if it belongs to the situation.
cells.ask: Say "that's mine" about one call you've been calling the room's, and let what you already know land without argument.
cells.core:
The compass works best when it's plainly yours — you feel what's right in the moment, say it once, and move. No polling the room, no waiting for the situation to announce what it wants. The pull toward light is easy to steer when the knowing isn't being outsourced.

That knowing is already sorting what's fair — in the gut, in the quiet judgments you make a dozen times a day. But it's described as if the room decided it, or the other person made it obvious. The credit has been going elsewhere while the compass runs. One plain act — saying out loud that a call was yours to make and you made it — returns the knowing to where it started. Fewer reasons, not more. What's true in you doesn't need a crowd.
